messages:
alice-cs: Hey team — Acme reported an incident this morning: duplicate token billing + partially duplicated generations after a quick reconnect in their browser client. They attached a repro and logs.

alice-cs: Short summary: user starts an SSE streaming generation, network blips, client reconnects immediately, receives a short partial response, then a second generation chunk arrives that appears to be a full restart of the same request. Customer got charged for both.

erin-customer: Repro steps we ran (from our SPA):
1) open stream with Authorization Bearer <token> and header X-Session-ID: sess-7
2) simulate network drop (chrome devtools) ~1s after stream starts
3) immediately reconnect with same X-Session-ID and same payload
4) we receive an extra generation and UI shows overlapping content.

erin-customer: Sample client logs: ``[2026-02-12T10:12:05Z] open stream id=abc123
[2026-02-12T10:12:06Z] received chunk seq=0 partial='Hello'
[2026-02-12T10:12:06Z] network error, retrying
[2026-02-12T10:12:07Z] reopen stream id=abc123 resume_token=rt-42
[2026-02-12T10:12:07Z] received chunk seq=0 partial='Hello'
[2026-02-12T10:12:07Z] received chunk seq=1 full='Hello, world!'
``

alice-cs: They included the HTTP traces — on the first connection we see an SSE ``event: chunk`` sequence with an interim chunk. After reconnect the server sent a new generation instead of resuming the KV/prefix.

ben-runtime: Thanks, digging in. A few clarifying q's: does the client include the resume token returned by the first connection when it reconnects? Or is it sending a fresh resume token? Also do you have the server-side request-ids (x-req-id) from the logs?

erin-customer: The client attempted to send the resume_token from the previous connection (rt-42). We attached request headers: ``x-req-id: rq-0a1b`` on the first connect and ``x-req-id: rq-0a1c`` on the reconnect.

carol-ml: Hypothesis: when resume_token rotates due to auth/session refresh we may be creating a new serving session server-side instead of attaching to the existing KV cache. That could cause the model to re-run generation and emit overlapping output. Need to check resume-token -> server-session mapping logic.

ben-runtime: I pulled the runtime logs for sess-7: we received resume_token=rt-42 on the second connect, but the code path that matches resume_token to a live session returned a MISS because the session map had an eviction (short TTL). Then fallback path spun up a fresh serving session for the incoming request. That explains the duplicate generation.

ben-runtime: Relevant log snippet: ``[runtime] match_resume: token=rt-42 -> MISS (evicted TTL=1.2s)
[runtime] spawn_session: new_sid=sess-7-2 model=redwood-1 quant=8bit
[serve] start_generation sid=sess-7-2 parent_req=rq-0a1c``

carol-ml: If session gets evicted that quickly we lose KV cache & prefix. On reconnect the runtime should do a resume-rehydrate from stored session snapshot rather than spawn a fresh session. This looks like TTL tuning + missing rehydrate path.

frank-prod: From a billing perspective this is bad — duplicates count as separate billed tokens. We should prioritize a mitigation: 1) server-side de-dupe by (customer_id + original_request_id + resume_token) for a short grace window; 2) recommend client backoff before immediate reconnect to allow resume lookup to complete.

alice-cs: Actionable next steps: ben, can you confirm TTL and whether the resume map eviction is aggressive? carol, is there a cheap change to prefer rehydrate over spawn when resume_token is present? frank, we'll draft a temporary customer note. I'll also ask Acme for a larger trace capturing the server x-req-ids.

ben-runtime: Confirmed: resume map TTL default is 1s (to conserve RAM on busy hosts) — that is too short for flaky mobile/web networks. I'll push a hotfix to 3s for the map and add a small synchronous rehydrate attempt before spawn (if resume_token present). Pushing PR now: ``#runtime/patch/rehydrate-resume``

ben-runtime: For immediate mitigation, we can also implement server-side idempotency check keyed by (customer_id, initial_client_request_digest) where digest = sha256(payload + user_session_id). That will reject duplicate spawn within 5s and respond with a resume hint.

carol-ml: Note: rehydrating KV across hosts may increase tail latency slightly. We'll gate the new behavior behind an opt-in flag and monitor latency for the next 48h.

frank-prod: Customer comms: draft OK — say we're investigating, cause likely session eviction during reconnect, mitigation in progress, temporary workaround: increase client backoff to 200-400ms before reconnect, and we'll provide a patch in the runtime.

erin-customer: Thanks. Quick question: would adding an idempotency-key on the client help? We can add that this afternoon if it reduces customer impact.

ben-runtime: Yes — adding a client-supplied idempotency-key (X-Idempotency-Key) that we check server-side will be effective immediately. If we see a repeated idempotency-key for the same customer within 10s we respond with the original stream resume and don't re-run the model. Recommend doing this now in your SDK.

alice-cs: dave-support-bot: can you attach the incident runbook link and create a short internal incident for priority=high? :exclamation:
